prompt: Why does TF-IDF give almost zero weight to the word 'the' in a collection of English documents?
options: Because 'the' is always removed by the tokenizer
Because 'the' appears in nearly every document, so its inverse document frequency is near zero
Because counts of 'the' are always zero
explanation: A word in almost every document has a document frequency close to N, so log(N / df) is close to zero.

prompt: Why is PPMI clipped at zero?
options: Because negative association is unreliable with sparse counts, and the positive part captures the informative pairs
Because the SVD requires non-negative inputs only
Because zero is the most common value
explanation: Co-occurrence counts are too sparse to estimate negative association reliably, so PPMI keeps only the positive part.

prompt: Why is cosine similarity preferred to Euclidean distance for comparing text vectors?
options: It is faster to compute on any vector
It compares direction and ignores length, so a long and a short text about the same topic still match
Euclidean distance cannot be computed for text
explanation: Text vectors often differ in magnitude because of length, and cosine focuses on the direction that carries the topic.

prompt: A search system returns the relevant document in position 4 for a query. What is its reciprocal rank?
explanation: The reciprocal rank is one divided by the position, so one quarter.

prompt: Why should search queries used for evaluation be kept separate from those used to tune the system?
options: Because tuning queries are always wrong
Because a system tuned on its own test queries looks better on them than it really is
Because evaluation queries must be longer
Because the ranking must be random during evaluation
explanation: Tuning on the evaluation queries fits the system to them, so the measured quality is optimistic.
